content.title: About
content.content: Marshmallows are soft confections made from sugar, syrup, gelatin, and whipped egg whites. They have a light, fluffy texture and a sweet taste, often coated in chocolate or dusted with powdered sugar. Marshmallows are popular as a snack, a baking ingredient, and a festive treat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Originally marshmallows were made from the sap of the marshmallow plant (Althaea officinalis).
Modern marshmallows use gelatin, but vegan versions exist using agar‑agar or pectin.
Marshmallows are a key component of the classic American dessert “s’mores” with chocolate and graham crackers.
In Japan, “fluffy” marshmallows are shaped into cute figures and flavored with a variety of tastes.
During space missions, marshmallows were used as a lightweight snack because they don’t crumble and store well.

items.title: Quick source of energy
items.content: The sugar in marshmallows is rapidly absorbed, providing an immediate glucose boost.

items.title: Lightweight snack
items.content: Low density makes them convenient for on‑the‑go consumption during active events.

items.title: Contains gelatin
items.content: Gelatin is rich in collagen, which supports skin, hair, and joint health.

items.title: Soothes the throat
items.content: Their soft texture and sweetness can ease discomfort from colds or irritated throats.

items.title: Flavor versatility
items.content: Marshmallows can be easily flavored, allowing the addition of vitamins and plant extracts.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption may contribute to weight gain, tooth decay, and blood sugar spikes.

items.title: Gelatin allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the gelatin used in traditional marshmallows.

items.title: Not suitable for vegans
items.content: Traditional products contain animal gelatin, so vegans should choose alternative versions.

items.title: Choking hazard for children
items.content: Soft yet sticky pieces can pose a choking risk for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Marshmallows can be enjoyed on their own, added to hot chocolate, used in baking, as cake decorations, or in s’mores. They can also be toasted over a flame for a caramelized exterior.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store marshmallows in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent melting and texture loss. Keep them away from moisture, which can make them sticky.
